title: 十二时辰水法 Shi'er shichen shuifa
subtitle: Xiyang Lou

model.line: Simple massing of a European palace: position and footprint from the ruin, the plan or a survey, heights read from the plates of the 1780s (research/xiyanglou/boxes.csv). Not a detailed model yet; the figures and their methods are in the Dimensions block.

evidence.title: Malone on the water clock and a later set in the palace
evidence.excerpt_other: The hydraulic machinery got out of order after the death of Father Benoit. No one could repair it and the water had to be raised more clumsily by buckets and ropes
evidence.summary: Malone's note also warns of a second set: bronze shichen in the Winter Palace, holding electric lights, said to have been made for the Empress Dowager Cixi and inferior to the plate's. So not every bronze zodiac figure in Beijing is from here.

evidence.title: Delatour on 海晏堂's jets, compared with Saint-Cloud and Versailles
evidence.excerpt_other: Ils produisent le même effet que les jets d'eau qui bordent la cascade de Saint-Cloud, ou ceux du perron qui, à Versailles, conduit de la fontaine du dragon à la terrasse.
evidence.summary: The basis of the Versailles comparisons. An effect, stated by a Paris reader of the plates. Same for Malone's 'buffets d'eaux' from Lettres édifiantes xxiv p.421, which is a Jesuit's own likeness. Both are comparisons of effect, never a statement that it was the model.

evidence.title: Plate X: 海晏堂 Haiyan Tang, west, and the water clock
evidence.excerpt_other: Sur deux des côtés du triangle, sont placés douze animaux de différentes espèces, six de chaque côté.
evidence.summary: Ten bays with a central block and attic and end pavilions; a landing with two stairs, jets from vases along both ramps as at St Cloud and Versailles. A triangular basin; animals spout towards the centre; at the apex towards the building a rock group with a shell; the largest jet from a vase at the base; two pyramids at the sides. He says animals spout by hour count.

evidence.title: Engraving 10: 海晏堂 Haiyan Tang, west front and water clock
evidence.excerpt_other: There two broad staircases one swinging to the right and one to the left, met before the main entrance on the level of the second floor.
evidence.summary: Largest of the group; held Benoist's pumps and the main reservoir. Fifty small jets on the stair balustrades fed three basins. Twelve seated animal figures, one for each two-hour period, spouted in turn to a larger fountain in the pool. After Benoist's death the machinery failed and water was raised by buckets and ropes (Benoist 1786, Amiot 1787, per n.). Malone compares bronze figures in the Winter Palace, made later.
